study type: Secondary analysis of a retrospective cohort study
cohort: The study included 18,589 patients with singleton, term deliveries who had umbilical artery cord gas available from the multicenter Consortium for Safe Labor dataset.
finding: Maternal diabetes, pre-eclampsia, placental abruption, and a history of prior Cesarean delivery were significantly associated with an increased likelihood of abnormal umbilical artery cord gas at delivery in singleton, term deliveries.
mod_finding: Both prior Cesarean delivery and current Cesarean delivery were associated with increased odds of having abnormal umbilical artery cord gas at delivery.
